Authors: Guo QJ, Liu Q, Bossi P, Bonomo P, Colevas AD, Lee NY, Lu TZ, Lee V, Mehanna H, Ng WT, et al.
Journal: The Lancet. Oncology | DOI: 10.1016/S1470-2045(26)00347-5
Published: 2026-Nov-01
PMID: 42933448



Abstract:
Patients with de novo metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma were historically deemed incurable and treated with palliative intent. Emergence of potent systemic therapy in combination with local treatment for both locoregional and metastatic diseases has enabled long-term survival in some patients. This international guideline was developed through consensus-building by 54 experts from 46 centres across 18 countries or regions and endorsed by 17 oncology organisations. 32 recommendations across seven clinical domains were formulated, including 29 strong (≥80% agreement [consensus] or high quality of evidence) and three conditional recommendations (67-79% agreement). We recommend that curative-intent treatment should be offered to medically fit patients with no more than three metastatic lesions in two or fewer organs at baseline or following response to systemic therapy; multimodality treatment (comprising immunochemotherapy, locoregional radiotherapy, metastasis-directed therapy, and maintenance therapy) is recommended. This guideline provides a practical framework for standardisation of clinical management of de novo metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma and identification of key evidence gaps for future research.

Authors: Tao K, Lin Z, Zhang P, Chi P, Xiao Y, Hou Z, Xu X, Zhang A, Qiu X, Wu J, et al.
Journal: The Lancet. Oncology | DOI: 10.1016/S1470-2045(26)00446-8
Published: 2026-Nov-01
PMID: 42927765



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: To our knowledge, UNION is the first phase 3 trial to assess a neoadjuvant strategy incorporating radiotherapy, immunotherapy, and chemotherapy compared with standard care in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer, which reported positive results for the primary endpoint (blinded independent review committee [BIRC]-assessed pathological complete response rate; 39·8% vs 15·3%). Here, we present a prespecified interim analysis of event-free survival. METHODS: This open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial was conducted at nine hospitals in China. Eligible patients were aged 18-75 years with untreated cT3-4 or N+ rectal adenocarcinoma (≤10 cm distance from the anal verge) and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0 or 1. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1; stratified by clinical T stage and N stage), using permuted blocks, to receive neoadjuvant short-course radiotherapy (25 Gy in five fractions) followed by two cycles of intravenous camrelizumab (200 mg on day 1) plus CAPOX (oral capecitabine 1000 mg/m2 twice daily on days 1-14 and intravenous oxaliplatin 130 mg/m2 on day 1; experimental group) or long-course chemoradiotherapy (50·4 Gy in 28 fractions with concurrent oral capecitabine 825 mg/m2 twice daily) followed by two cycles of CAPOX (standard-of-care group). After surgery, both groups received six cycles of adjuvant CAPOX, and the experimental group additionally received adjuvant camrelizumab for up to 15 cycles. The primary endpoint was BIRC-assessed pathological complete response rate in the intention-to-treat population, which has been previously reported. Here, we performed a prespecified interim analysis of investigator-assessed event-free survival (one of the key secondary endpoints, defined as time from randomisation to radiographic progression precluding surgery, local recurrence or distant metastasis, or death) in the intention-to-treat population (all randomly assigned patients) with a boundary of a two-sided p values less than 0·0102. Safety was evaluated in all patients who received at least one dose of the study treatment according to the assigned regimen. The study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04928807, and is active, but no longer recruiting. FINDINGS: Between July 23, 2021, and March 1, 2023, 231 patients (153 [66%] males and 78 [34%] females; 227 [98%] were Han Chinese, and four [2%] were other ethnicity Chinese) were randomly assigned to the experimental group (n=113) and standard-of-care group (n=118). As of Oct 1, 2025, the median follow-up duration was 36·7 months (IQR 32·6-39·9) in the experimental group and 34·7 months (31·1-39·1) in the standard-of-care group. The 3-year investigator-assessed event-free survival rate was 91·3% (95% CI 83·9-95·4) in the experimental group versus 77·4% (67·9-84·4) in the standard-of-care group (stratified hazard ratio 0·33 [0·15-0·71]; two-sided log-rank p=0·0029). During the entire treatment period, the most common grade 3 or 4 treatment-related adverse events were decreased lymphocyte count (23 [20%] of 115 in the experimental group vs 31 [28%] of 112 in the standard-of-care group), decreased white blood cell count (13 [11%] vs 16 [14%]), decreased neutrophil count (13 [11%] vs 13 [12%]), and decreased platelet count (seven [6%] vs 15 [13%]). Treatment-related serious adverse events occurred in 22 (19%) versus 15 (13%) patients, with the most common being decreased platelet count (one [1%] vs six [5%]), and radiation gastroenteritis (two [2%] vs four [4%]). Treatment-related deaths occurred in one patient in the experimental group (septic shock related to chemotherapy, but unrelated to camrelizumab) and none in the standard-of-care group. INTERPRETATION: In this interim analysis, short-course radiotherapy followed by camrelizumab and CAPOX significantly improved 3-year event-free survival in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer, with a safety profile similar to long-course chemoradiotherapy followed by CAPOX. Comparison of this promising new treatment strategy with contemporary total neoadjuvant therapy strategies is warranted. FUNDING: Key Clinical Research Initiative Program of Union Hospital, National Key Technology Research and Development Programme of Hubei Province, and Jiangsu Hengrui Pharmaceuticals. TRANSLATION: For the Chinese translation of the abstract see Supplementary Materials section.

Authors: Paris J, Tsimiklis J, Agarwal A, Tong JY, Selva D
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70533
Published: 2026-Oct-29
PMID: 42958743



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Immunotherapy is increasingly used for head and neck cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC) with perineural spread (PNS), though outcomes remain poorly defined. METHODS: A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA and MOOSE guidelines. Studies reporting immunotherapy in cSCC with clinical or radiologic cranial nerve PNS were included. Data on demographics, nerve involvement, treatment, response, and outcomes were extracted. RESULTS: Twenty-three studies (150 patients) were included. Median age was 72.5 years; 78.5% were male. PNS most commonly involved CNV (83.3%) and CNVII (31.7%). Immunotherapy was primarily cemiplimab (75.2%) and pembrolizumab (19.7%). Disease control was achieved in 87.3% (complete response: 38.7%, partial response: 42.0%). Functional nerve recovery was reported in 26/64 patients with evaluable outcomes (40.6%), equivalent to 17.3% of the total cohort. Median follow-up was 16 months, with 82.3% alive. Adverse events occurred in 28%, with serious toxicity rare. CONCLUSIONS: The available evidence demonstrates that immunotherapy can achieve disease control in cSCC with PNS and that established cranial nerve dysfunction may recover in some patients. Prospective studies with standardized oncological and functional outcomes are needed to better define treatment efficacy and establish the role of immunotherapy within current treatment paradigms.

Authors: Bai Y, Cheng H, Zhou Y, Zhou J, Thirunavukarasu A, Ke Y, Yao J, Fukutsu K, Quek CWN, Hong ASY, et al.
Journal: Nature medicine | DOI: 10.1038/s41591-026-04655-5
Published: 2026-Oct-29
PMID: 42957777



Abstract:
Despite their considerable promise, many current medical foundation models remain modality specific and lack transparent reasoning, limiting clinical adoption. To address this gap, we introduce Explainable Vision Language Foundation Model for Medicine (EVLF-FM), a multimodal vision language foundation model that combines broad diagnostic capabilities with fine-grained explainability. The development and testing of EVLF-FM encompassed more than 1.3 million total samples from 18 global datasets across 10 imaging modalities related to six clinical specialties: dermatology, hepatology, ophthalmology, pathology, pulmonology and radiology. External validation employed 13,443 independent test samples from 17 additional datasets across 10 imaging modalities. EVLF-FM supports disease diagnosis, visual question answering and pixel-level visual grounding with reasoning capabilities. In internal validation for disease diagnostics, EVLF-FM achieved the highest average accuracy, 0.895, outperforming leading generalist and specialist models. In medical visual grounding, EVLF-FM also achieved reasonable performance across nine modalities with average accuracy at 0.5 intersection over union (Acc@0.5) of 0.842. External testing further confirmed consistent zero-shot and few-shot performance, with competitive F1 scores despite a smaller model size. A hybrid training strategy combining supervised and visual reinforcement fine-tuning enables EVLF-FM to generate clinically interpretable explanations aligned with visual evidence. Human evaluation of these reasoning outputs using the S.C.O.R.E. framework yielded a high overall mean score of 4.25/5, supporting their clinical interpretability. Current limitations include the need for additional validation across diverse healthcare settings. Prospective clinical studies are required to evaluate the safety, effectiveness and clinical utility of EVLF-FM before routine clinical deployment.

Authors: Li Z, Zhang Y, Luo W, Jing Y, Yu Q, Song Y, Lu W, Xia S, Chen X, Yu H, et al.
Journal: Oncogene | DOI: 10.1038/s41388-026-04030-1
Published: 2026-Oct-29
PMID: 42957743



Abstract:
The IL-36γ/IL-36R signaling axis mediates cellular communication in various contexts and has recently been implicated in pro-fibrotic responses. However, its specific role in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), which is characterized by abundant cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), remains elusive. Here, we investigated the contribution of IL-36γ/IL-36R signaling to CAF function and OSCC progression. Immunohistochemical analysis of patient samples revealed that IL-36γ was highly expressed in CAFs and that higher co-expression of IL-36γ/IL-36R in CAFs was associated with more invasive patterns and shorter disease-free survival. By integrating tumor cell lines with patient-derived organoids (PDOs), we established three co-culture systems to model these interactions. These models revealed that IL-36γ signaling enhanced CAF proliferation and extracellular matrix remodeling. Mechanistically, the IL-36γ/IL-36R axis in CAFs increased ERK1/2-dependent CCL20 secretion, which in turn promoted tumor cell invasion. Pharmacological blockade of IL-36R attenuated both the IL-36γ-induced increase in CAF abundance and the associated pro-tumorigenic CAF phenotypes in vivo. Collectively, these findings suggest that the IL-36γ/IL-36R-ERK1/2-CCL20 signaling cascade participates in CAF-tumor interactions. Targeting IL-36R may therefore represent a promising therapeutic strategy for invasive OSCC.

Authors: Bergen S, Henderson MM, Reverby SM
Journal: American journal of public health | DOI: 10.2105/AJPH.2026.308773
Published: 2026-Oct-29
PMID: 42956371



Abstract:
We examine the material and conceptual impact of the Coalition for the Reproductive Rights of Workers (CRROW) during the late 1970s. CRROW assembled in response to the news that five women had undergone sterilization procedures to retain their unionized industrial jobs at an American Cyanamid chemical manufacturing plant in Willow Island, West Virginia, following the plant's institution of a so-called fetal protection policy. Drawing on organizational archives and oral histories, we piece together the trajectory of CRROW, highlighting its promise in bridging political divides between unionized labor, feminists and reproductive rights activists, and environmentalists, as well as its shortcomings in putting its aims into practice as the occupational health regulations built out in the 1970s fell victim to the changing political headwinds of the 1980s. Throughout, we emphasize the lessons CRROW, in its successes and its limitations, offers health advocates in the present. (Am J Public Health. Published online ahead of print October 29, 2026:e1-e7. https://doi.org/10.2105/AJPH.2026.308773).

Authors: Gong X, Qi X, Feng M, Zhu L, Wang N
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0360296
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42956049



Abstract:
Long-cable PWM-driven induction motor electric submersible pump (ESP) systems suffer from significant voltage reflection issues caused by distributed parameter effects, leading to transient overvoltages at the motor terminals that can reach several times the DC bus voltage. This severely threatens system stability and motor insulation integrity, and traditional control methods prove inadequate for effective suppression. To address this challenge, the paper proposes an improved model predictive current control (MPCC) strategy for induction motor ESP systems, which integrates overvoltage suppression and equivalent switching frequency reduction for long-cable PWM-driven applications. The reflection overvoltage mechanism is thoroughly analyzed through mathematical modeling of the motor and long-cable transmission line, and the applicability of predictive current control in such systems is investigated. The core improvement lies in a circular boundary constrained MPCC combined with a dynamic transition voltage vector selection mechanism, which enables dual-mode optimization based on current error boundary conditions: the normal cost function is applied within the circular boundary to jointly optimize voltage tracking, switching frequency, and dv/dt; while the backup cost function is activated outside the boundary to prioritize current error minimization. This effectively optimizes the voltage switching strategy, reducing both switching frequency and dv/dt, thereby preventing overvoltage excitation caused by abrupt voltage vector steps in PWM-driven systems. Simulation models under different cable configurations (1 km with RLC filter and 110 m without RLC filter) and an experimental platform based on a neutral-point-clamped three-level inverter (NPC-TLI) topology are established, with the 110 m no-filter configuration serving as a direct cross-validation baseline. Comparative simulation and experimental results demonstrate that the proposed strategy significantly reduces the duration of motor terminal overvoltage while maintaining excellent system dynamic performance. Moreover, the improved MPCC effectively suppresses overvoltage and reduces equivalent switching frequency without requiring hardware filter redesign, while the RLC filter remains necessary for full insulation safety compliance under more demanding long-cable conditions, substantially mitigating the risk of motor insulation breakdown.

Authors: Şimşekoğlu N, Arslanoğlu İ, Portakal B, Aktaş S
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0361574
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42956008



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Achieving early glycemic control in adolescents with diabetes is associated with improved short- and long-term health outcomes. The aim of this study was to examine the relationship between eating attitudes and glycemic control, as well as the factors associated with eating attitudes and glycemic control, in adolescents with diabetes. METHODS: This descriptive cross-sectional study included 143 adolescents with diabetes, aged 10-19 years, who attended a research hospital between February and April 2024. The data were collected using a Descriptive Information Form, Eating Attitudes Test (EAT) and an information form questioning the values of some metabolic variables. RESULTS: The mean age of the participants was 14 ± 2.3 years and 49.7% had diabetes between 1-5 years. The mean total score of the EAT scale was 16.62 ± 8.30. The mean score of the "Dieting" subscale of the EAT scale was 10.39 ± 5.58, the mean score of the "Bulimia food preoccupation" subscale was 2.33 ± 3.03 and the mean score of the "Oral Control" subscale was 3.79 ± 3.08. There was no significant difference between the mean EAT total score and glycemic control. CONCLUSIONS: The mean EAT-26 total score was below the commonly used cutoff score, and no significant association was found between EAT-26 scores and HbA1c. Differences in EAT-26 total and subscale scores were observed according to selected demographic and clinical characteristics, including BMI, treatment modality, and treatment adherence. These findings describe self-reported eating attitudes in the study sample and support the inclusion of eating-related assessment within the holistic care of adolescents with Type 1 DM.

Authors: He L, Huang X, Huang P
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0361607
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42955997



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is a common head and neck cancer, and radiotherapy is its main treatment. Recurrence and metastasis are the main causes of treatment failure. Although immunotherapy can prolong patient survival, the molecular mechanisms underlying NPC development and progression remain unclear. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) and their target genes are abnormally expressed in many tumors and are closely involved in tumor development. Therefore, this study aimed to identify key miRNAs and immune-related target genes in NPC, construct miRNA-mRNA regulatory networks, and screen for and validate core immune genes to identify prognostic molecular biomarkers for NPC. METHODS: We downloaded NPC-related miRNA (GSE32960) and mRNA (GSE12452, GSE13597, GSE64634) microarray datasets from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) and identified differentially expressed miRNAs (DEMs) and mRNAs (DEGs) using R. Target genes of DEMs were predicted with TargetScan, miRDB, and miRWalk, and then intersected with DEGs to identify core genes. A miRNA-mRNA regulatory network was constructed in Cytoscape. The core genes were further overlapped with immune-related gene sets, followed by functional enrichment analysis. A prognostic risk model was established using LASSO-Cox regression, and immune cell infiltration was evaluated with CIBERSORT. Model validation, immunohistochemical analysis, and drug-gene interaction analysis were also performed. In vitro, RT-qPCR was conducted in C666-1 and NP69 cell lines to verify the expression of key genes. RESULTS: We identified 213 potential target genes of key miRNAs. Three miRNAs (hsa-miR-30e-5p, hsa-miR-30a-5p, and hsa-miR-20a-5p) were associated with NPC prognosis, and 17 core immune-related genes were enriched in cytokine-mediated signaling, chemokine response, and JAK-STAT pathways. Five genes (CXCL11, SOCS1, ROBO1, LGR5, and RORB) showed promising diagnostic value for NPC; their expression was positively correlated (P < 0.05) with CD8 ⁺ T-cell, macrophage, and neutrophil infiltration. Drug-gene analysis predicted that 5-fluorouracil targeted LGR5 and aldesleukin targeted SOCS1. RT-qPCR demonstrated that SOCS1 was upregulated approximately 3.7-fold in NPC cells (P < 0.01). CONCLUSION: This study identified potential novel key genes in nasopharyngeal carcinoma, providing new therapeutic targets for the treatment of this disease.

Authors: Fleming GE, Roth H, Hanna GJ, Sethi RKV, Minken J, Mukundan D, Schoenfeld JD, Windon MJ, Rettig EM
Journal: JAMA otolaryngology-- head & neck surgery | DOI: 10.1001/jamaoto.2026.3379
Published: 2026-Oct-29
PMID: 42955024



Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Circulating tumor human papillomavirus DNA (ctHPVDNA) is a potential biomarker for surveillance of HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancer. Despite its growing clinical use, patient experiences are not well characterized, and understanding patient perspectives of ctHPVDNA-guided surveillance is essential to guiding its appropriate use while mitigating potential harms. OBJECTIVE: To characterize patient experiences with ctHPVDNA-guided surveillance. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: A mixed-methods cross-sectional interview study in adults treated for HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancer with 1 or more surveillance ctHPVDNA test 3 or more months before enrollment conducted in June through August 2025 in a single tertiary academic cancer center. Purposive sampling ensured representation of diverse patient experiences. EXPOSURES: One semistructured interview regarding experiences with ctHPVDNA-guided surveillance. Willingness to pay (WTP) out of pocket was assessed using iterative bidding. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Themes and subthemes were derived from coded interview transcripts using a categorical inductive approach. RESULTS: Among 20 participants (median age, 58 years [IQR, 55-70 years]; 16 males [80%]), 8 (40%) had true-negative ctHPVDNA test results, 6 had true-positive results (30%), 4 had false-negative results (20%), and 2 had false-positive results (10%). Five major themes emerged: (1) broad enthusiasm and support for ctHPVDNA testing, with a common assumption that more and earlier disease-related information is beneficial, and appreciation for the reassurance of negative test results (discordance between support for testing in general and personal experiences of test accuracy was observed); (2) distress as inherent to the emotional variability of the cancer journey itself, such that anxiety associated with ctHPVDNA testing was considered attributable to cancer survivorship rather than to the test; (3) trust in the oncology team supersedes trust in test itself, whereby clinicians were trusted to appropriately interpret potentially confusing results (this trust was enhanced by clear communication); (4) test as a valuable add-on to standard care, which should enrich, but not replace, standard surveillance; and (5) sensitivity to financial toxicity, with strong support for accessible and equitable testing. The median per-test WTP was $325 (range, $0-$9000). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This study found that participants expressed strong support for ctHPVDNA-guided surveillance. Trust in clinicians appeared to mitigate distress related to confusing or inaccurate test results. Clinicians using ctHPVDNA testing should be familiar with and clearly communicate its strengths and limitations to optimize clinical benefit.
